root_cause.text: `amdgpu_cs_parser_bos()` failed to unwind its mutex-locked/error path when `amdgpu_hmm_range_alloc()` returned `NULL` under low-memory conditions, causing an incomplete cleanup path in the AMDGPU CS BO parsing code.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (unlikely(!e->range)) return -ENOMEM;` to `r = -ENOMEM; goto out_free_user_pages;`, and the commit message explicitly says “In low memory conditions, kmalloc can fail. In such conditions unlock the mutex for a clean exit,” showing the bug was a missing cleanup/unlock on allocation failure in `drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_cs.c`.

Author: Sunil Khatri <sunil.khatri@amd.com>

    drm/amdgpu: use user provided hmm_range buffer in amdgpu_ttm_tt_get_user_pages
    
    update the amdgpu_ttm_tt_get_user_pages and all dependent function
    along with it callers to use a user allocated hmm_range buffer instead
    hmm layer allocates the buffer.
    
    This is a need to get hmm_range pointers easily accessible
    without accessing the bo a
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown code allocates the HMM range buffer before calling into user-page pinning: `e->range = kzalloc(sizeof(*e->range), GFP_KERNEL); if (unlikely(!e->range)) return -ENOMEM;` and then passes that buffer with `r = amdgpu_ttm_tt_get_user_pages(bo, e->range);`. This change means the function no longer depends on an internal `amdgpu_hmm_range_alloc()` path that could return NULL and leave the mutex/error unwind incomplete. The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is therefore not present here, and the fix (user-allocated HMM range buffer plus explicit allocation failure handling) is already in place.
